what: App hardening makes a mobile banking app harder to fake, tamper with or spy on. The app collects an integrity proof from the OS (Play Integrity, App Attest), pins its server certificate, and the server judges the result and ends idle sessions.
like: Like a bank checking the courier's ID badge and the sealed envelope before accepting a delivery, then closing the window if nobody speaks for a few minutes.
why: Blocks fake or modified apps from calling your API
Pinning makes man-in-the-middle proxies fail on the device
Server-side timeouts protect accounts even if the app is stolen or left open

steps.d: OWASP MASVS groups controls into STORAGE, CRYPTO, AUTH, NETWORK, PLATFORM, CODE, RESILIENCE and PRIVACY, so you can say what you cover and why.

steps.t: Ask the OS for an attestation
steps.d: Play Integrity returns device, app and account verdicts; App Check wraps Play Integrity, App Attest or DeviceCheck into a token your backend can validate.
The backend checks the nonce or requestHash to stop replay, then appRecognitionVerdict and licensing, then device labels. Never trust a verdict decided inside the app.
Allow, allow with limits, step-up or deny, rather than a hard block. Run in telemetry mode first to see false positives.
Pin SubjectPublicKeyInfo hashes in the network security config, always include a backup pin, and consider an expiry so a missed rotation cannot lock users out.
Idle timeout 2-5 minutes for high-value apps and an absolute timeout, both kept server-side because client timers can be manipulated.

numbers.l: default Play Integrity request quota across all installs, extendable on request
typical Play Integrity standard request latency (classic takes a few seconds)
common idle timeout for high-value applications (15-30 min for low-risk)

choices.d: Standard is the recommended default: faster and replay-protected by Google Play. Classic fits rare, high-value checks but you must manage the nonce.

choices.t: Pin the leaf, the key or a CA
choices.d: Pinning public key hashes with a backup pin survives certificate renewal; pinning only a leaf risks outages. Without a backup pin you need an app update to recover.
Tiered responses such as limits or a CAPTCHA reduce harm to legitimate users on odd devices. Collect telemetry first.
Root or jailbreak checks in the app can be hooked and bypassed. Use them as signals; the decision belongs on the server.

instead.why: The web counterpart for stopping injected script and data theft
Session and token design that the idle and absolute timeouts apply to

breaks.d: The pinned key rotates and the app has no second pin.
breaks.see: All requests fail until users update
breaks.fix: Backup pin, expiry, and a staged rollout plan for key changes

breaks.d: The app decides if the device is fine.
breaks.fix: Send the token to the backend and enforce there

breaks.d: A timer in the app logs the user out.
breaks.fix: Server-side idle and absolute expiry on every token

say: I map the app to OWASP MASVS and treat resilience features as defence in depth, not the main control.
Integrity tokens from Play Integrity or App Check are verified on the server with a nonce, and the response is tiered rather than a hard block.
I pin public keys with a backup pin, and idle timeouts of a few minutes are enforced on the server.

followups.a: No. It raises effort, but code on the device can be modified. Use signals plus server-side controls, short-lived tokens and step-up for risky actions.

followups.q: What breaks if you pin wrongly?
followups.a: Users cannot connect after a certificate or key change. Mitigate with backup pins, pin-set expiry, and planned rotation.

today: Attestation moved to server-judged verdicts: Play Integrity standard requests and Firebase App Check. Android's own docs warn pinning limits flexibility, so teams pin keys with backups and roll out carefully.

check.q: Where should an integrity verdict be judged?
check.why: Client-side checks can be bypassed on a compromised device.
Without a backup pin a key change needs an app update.
OWASP says timeout management must be enforced server-side.
